T: Seven deadly sins. Seven ways to die.
D: A detective a week from retirement and his hot-headed new partner hunt a killer working through the seven deadly sins, in a city where it never stops raining.
P: Serve the spaghetti when Somerset and Mills walk into Monday's crime scene.
S: Thin griddled mini cheeseburgers. People wanna eat cheeseburgers, lotto and television.

Shape the mince into 8 thin patties a little wider than the buns and season with salt and pepper. Sear in a very hot pan for 2 minutes, flip, add the cheese and cook a minute more. Toast the buns, then build with mustard, tomato sauce, onion, pickle and a patty. Serve on a plate in front of the television.
Crunchy beef tacos with hot sauce
Corn shells of spiced ground beef, lettuce and cheese, hot sauce. Mills wasn't guarding Taco Bell.

Brown the mince with the onion, breaking it up. Stir in the spices, oregano, tomato paste and half a cup of water and simmer until thick. Warm the shells in a 180C oven for 5 minutes. Fill with the mince, lettuce, cheese and tomato and shake on the hot sauce.
M: Monday's spaghetti and meatballs in red sauce
Beef and pork meatballs in red sauce over spaghetti, pace yourself.

Mix the beef, pork, breadcrumbs, egg, parmesan and a clove of garlic, season and roll into 20 small balls. Brown the meatballs in the oil, then lift out. Soften the onion and the rest of the garlic in the same pan, add the tomatoes and oregano and bring to a simmer. Return the meatballs and simmer gently, half covered, until the sauce is thick. Boil the spaghetti, toss with some sauce and basil, and serve with the meatballs and extra parmesan.
40g parmesan, grated, plus extra to serve@Dairy
Roast chicken for Wednesday night, while the subway rattles the flat.

Mix the butter, garlic, lemon zest and thyme leaves and push it under the chicken skin, then put the halved lemon inside. Roast the chicken at 200C with the oiled potatoes around it, turning the potatoes once, until the juices run clear. Rest the chicken, then stir the flour into the pan juices on the stove and whisk in the stock until it bubbles into gravy. Carve and serve with the potatoes and gravy.
W: Dark chocolate truffles dusted in cocoa, packed into a plain box.

Bring the cream to a simmer, pour it over the chocolate and butter, wait a minute, then stir until smooth. Chill until firm enough to scoop. Roll teaspoons of the mix into balls, toss half in cocoa and top the rest with a few salt flakes. Pack into the box, write FRAGILE on the lid and hand it over at 7pm.
K: Wine for Somerset at Tracy's table.
Open the wine an hour ahead. Pour into 4 large glasses and serve at cool room temperature.
